64	
65	### 2.1 Single purpose (single-purpose description field)

67	their open browser tabs as a visual, spatial workspace. Every permission and

69	browser data the user opts into, and to personalize the new-tab surface.

101	  approved use cases.
102	- ☑ I do **not** use or transfer user data for purposes unrelated to my item's
103	  single purpose.
104	- ☑ I do **not** use or transfer user data to determine creditworthiness or for

108	`https://emberstone-studio.com/docs/privacy/`
109	
110	This is a catch-all Emberstone Studio policy, not Meridian-specific text, and it
111	is not yet a reliable substitute for `PRIVACY.md`'s Meridian-specific
112	disclosures (see the accuracy gaps below). **[OWNER ACTION STILL NEEDED]**

124	## 3. Data handling disclosure (paste-ready listing block)
125	
126	Meridian processes the following **locally in your browser** to provide its
127	features. Most of it stays in on-device storage; preferences are the exception
128	and can sync through your own Chrome Sync account (see "Local & sync storage"
129	below):
130	
131	- **Browsing activity** — open tab titles, URLs, domains, tab-group membership,
132	  and tab activation/order, used to display, search, and manage your tabs. A
133	  local search index and workspace/UI state are stored in `chrome.storage.local`.
134	- **Website content** — after a page loads, Meridian reads its meta description
135	  and H1/H2 headings so local search can match page context beyond the title and
136	  URL. It does not read form input or other page-body text.
137	- **Screenshots** — Meridian captures the visible area of active tabs after tab
138	  activation or page load, and during a user-requested full refresh that cycles
139	  eligible tabs. Automatic captures (activation/page load) do not filter by URL
140	  in Meridian's code — Chrome's `captureVisibleTab` API itself refuses
141	  `chrome://`, Chrome Web Store, and other extensions' pages, so only those
142	  attempts fail; any other page, including one with sensitive content on
143	  screen, is captured. The full refresh additionally skips `chrome://`,
144	  `chrome-extension://`, and `about:` tabs in Meridian's own code before
145	  switching to them. Screenshots are stored as JPEG blobs in extension-local
146	  IndexedDB; cache metadata and refresh markers use `chrome.storage.local`.
147	  Storage targets roughly 200 entries / ~50 MB and
148	  prunes the oldest thumbnails first, but a still-open tab's thumbnail is never
149	  evicted to make room, so usage can exceed that target while those tabs stay
150	  open. A tab's thumbnail is removed when the tab closes.
151	- **Local & sync storage** — preferences (theme, background, search provider,
152	  enabled local-search sources, new-tab behavior, optional homepage, domain
153	  grouping) are stored in `chrome.storage.sync`. If the user has Chrome Sync
154	  turned on, Chrome syncs this data through the user's own Google/Chrome
155	  account to their other signed-in devices, subject to the user's Chrome Sync
156	  settings — it is not Meridian-operated syncing. Workspaces, search metadata,
157	  thumbnails, the Meridian/previous tab IDs, and an uploaded custom background
158	  image stay in `chrome.storage.local` / IndexedDB and are not synced.
159	- **Optional bookmarks & history** — off by default. Meridian requests bookmark
160	  or history access only when you enable that source in Settings → Local Search
161	  or select its search scope, and queries it only to show local-search results.
162	  It keeps no separate persistent copy; revoking access turns the source off.
163	- **External requests** — search-provider icons load from fixed Google,
164	  DuckDuckGo, Bing, and Brave icon URLs (these contain no visited URL); favicons
165	  resolve through Chrome's packaged `_favicon` provider (not Google S2); the
166	  background settings load photo previews and selected photos from
167	  `picsum.photos` by seed. Starting a web search, opening a result, or choosing a
168	  custom homepage navigates your browser to that destination normally.
169	- **Retention & deletion** — data persists in local/sync storage until replaced,
170	  evicted, cleared, or removed with the extension or profile. Closing a tab
171	  deletes its cached thumbnail and search entry (including extracted metadata).
172	  You can clear all extension data through Chrome's controls.
173	- **Outbound links in Settings** — the Settings panel's Emberstone Studio
174	  footer contains two static links: the studio site
175	  (`https://emberstone-studio.com`) and a Ko-fi donation page
176	  (`https://ko-fi.com/emberstonestudio`). They do nothing until the user
177	  explicitly clicks one, which opens that destination in a new tab. Meridian
178	  makes no background request for them and adds no click tracking or analytics.
179	- **No telemetry or backend** — Meridian has no Meridian-operated server, no
180	  analytics or advertising SDK, no account system, and no telemetry uploader.

184	## 4. Permission justifications
185	
186	Paste each string into the matching "why do you need this permission?" field.
187	
188	### Required permissions
189	
190	**`tabs`**
191	Read tab titles, URLs, domains, and group/window membership and act on tabs
192	(activate, close, move, group, restore) so Meridian can render the new-tab page's
193	tab cards, power local tab search, and manage tabs from its UI.
194	
195	**`tabGroups`**
196	Read and manage Chrome tab groups so Meridian's workspace lanes reflect and can
197	modify tab-group membership and grouping.
198	
199	**`storage`**
200	Persist the user's preferences, workspaces, tab-search index (including extracted
201	page metadata), thumbnail cache metadata, and tab-tracking state in
202	`chrome.storage.local`/`chrome.storage.sync`, plus JPEG thumbnail blobs in
203	IndexedDB, so settings and layout survive across sessions.
204	
205	**`unlimitedStorage`**
206	Screenshot thumbnails are stored as JPEG blobs in IndexedDB and can exceed the
207	default storage quota. `unlimitedStorage` lets the local thumbnail cache hold enough
208	entries to be useful. Code targets roughly 200 entries / ~50 MB and prunes the
209	oldest thumbnails first when over that target, but never evicts a thumbnail for
210	a tab that is still open — so actual usage can exceed the target while those
211	tabs stay open.
212	
213	**`favicon`**
214	Display site icons for tabs and search results by resolving page URLs through
215	Chrome's packaged `_favicon` provider, avoiding third-party favicon lookups.
216	
217	**`sidePanel`**
218	Provide Meridian's side-panel UI, which opens when the toolbar icon is clicked.
219	
220	**`scripting`**
221	After an open tab finishes loading, run a one-shot extractor that reads only that
222	page's meta description and H1/H2 heading text into the local tab-search index,
223	so local search can match page context beyond the title and URL. It does not read
224	form input or other page-body content. `scripting` (rather than click-scoped
225	`activeTab`) is required because this indexing happens automatically on page
226	load, not from a user click.
227	
228	**`host_permissions: <all_urls>`**
229	Allow two automatic, non-click actions across the tabs the user already has open:
230	(1) capturing the visible tab via `captureVisibleTab` after tab activation, after
231	a page finishes loading, and during a user-requested full refresh, to build
232	thumbnail cards; and (2) running the load-time meta/H1/H2 metadata extractor
233	above. Chrome's click-scoped `activeTab` cannot authorize these automatic
234	background actions, so broad host access is required for the shipped
235	live-thumbnail and auto-indexing behavior. Neither automatic action filters by
236	URL in Meridian's own code; Chrome's `captureVisibleTab` and `scripting` APIs
237	refuse to act on `chrome://`, Chrome Web Store, and other extensions' pages, so
238	those are excluded by Chrome's own restrictions, not by a Meridian allowlist.
239	The separate, user-requested full refresh does explicitly skip `chrome://`,
240	`chrome-extension://`, and `about:` tabs in Meridian's code before switching to
241	them. Meridian makes no network request to a Meridian server.
242	
243	### Optional permissions (requested only on demand)
244	
245	**`bookmarks`** *(optional)*
246	Requested only when the user enables bookmark search in Settings → Local Search
247	or selects the bookmark scope. Used to read bookmark titles, URLs, and folder
248	names to return local-search results. No persistent copy of the bookmark tree is
249	created; denying or revoking it leaves the feature off.
250	
251	**`history`** *(optional)*
252	Requested only when the user enables history search in Settings → Local Search or
253	selects the history scope. Used to read history titles, URLs, and visit times to
254	return local-search results. No persistent history database is created; denying
255	or revoking it leaves the feature off.
256

269	  Meridian-specific disclosures — see §2.4 for the required additions before
270	  this can be entered in the store dashboard as-is.
271	- **[OWNER-ONLY — NOT DONE]** Enter and submit the single-purpose description,
272	  data-type selections, and the three data-usage certifications in the dashboard.
273	- **[OWNER-ONLY — NOT DONE]** Confirm each permission justification against the
274	  exact uploaded archive and paste it into the dashboard field.
275	- **[OWNER-ONLY — NOT DONE]** Verify prominent-disclosure / affirmative-consent
276	  requirements for screenshot capture and optional bookmarks/history are met in
277	  the listing and in-product experience (a policy link alone may not suffice).
278	- **[OWNER-ONLY — NOT DONE]** Perform a manual network audit of the packed
279	  release (new-tab, side panel, settings, search, bookmark/history,
280	  missing-favicon, thumbnail-refresh flows) and confirm no analytics, telemetry,
281	  or remote code beyond this repository.
282	- **[OWNER-ONLY — NOT DONE]** Review the current `picsum.photos` and
283	  search-provider policies/terms, and Chrome's favicon-endpoint guidance, for
284	  ongoing accuracy.
285	- **[OWNER-ONLY — NOT DONE]** Reconcile support-contact details, retention/
286	  deletion statements, and all store-form answers with actual operational
287	  practice.
288	
289	---
290	
291	## 6. Reconciliation notes
292	
293	Verified against the current source on the "Last updated" date:
294	
295	- **Manifest ↔ copy** — required permissions (`tabs`, `tabGroups`, `storage`,
296	  `unlimitedStorage`, `scripting`, `sidePanel`, `favicon`), optional
297	  (`bookmarks`, `history`), and host access (`<all_urls>`) each have a
298	  justification above. The repository root manifest and `meridian-extension/`
299	  manifest are identical.
300	- **Runtime ↔ copy** — screenshots are JPEG blobs in IndexedDB after
301	  `captureVisibleTab` (quality 72) and bounded resizing; a display failure keeps
302	  the stored blob and marks it for replacement on a later natural activation;
303	  the cache targets a soft ~200 entries / ~50 MB, pruning the oldest thumbnails
304	  first but never evicting a still-open tab's thumbnail, and always evicting on
305	  tab close (`utils/thumbnailCache.js`); automatic capture (activation/page
306	  load) does not filter by URL in code and relies on Chrome's own
307	  `captureVisibleTab`/`scripting` restrictions, while the user-requested full
308	  refresh explicitly skips `chrome://`, `chrome-extension://`, and `about:`
309	  tabs (`background.js`); the extractor reads meta description + H1/H2 only
310	  (`utils/browserSearch.js`); favicons use the `_favicon` endpoint
311	  (`utils/favicon.js`); background photos use `picsum.photos` seeds
312	  (`components/SettingsPanel.js`, 12 photos); the Settings Emberstone Studio
313	  footer adds two static outbound links (studio site + Ko-fi donation page)
314	  that only navigate on explicit user click, with no click tracking or
315	  analytics (`components/SettingsPanel.js`); `chrome.storage.sync` preference
316	  data can sync through the user's own Chrome Sync account. No backend/
317	  telemetry code exists.
318	- **Terminology** — "workspace lanes," "local search," "thumbnails/screenshots,"
319	  and "optional bookmarks/history" are used consistently in `README.md`,
320	  `PRIVACY.md`, and this document.
